notes: §1985:XI.4.4.3 SR7 is a permission: 'The files referenced by file-name-2 and file-name-3 may reside on the same multiple file reel.' FileControlBinder.ScreenMultipleFileClause records each MULTIPLE FILE TAPE clause's files as FileModel.MultipleFileReels (§1985:VII.2.11.3 GR1), and the one reader that refuses same-reel files in a sort verb, SortBinder.ScreenMultipleFileReels (§1985:XI.4.1.3 SR6, COBOL6815), is called from BindMerge only; SortBindFile never calls it, so a SORT whose USING and GIVING files share a reel compiles and runs at 85. Probes at --std 85: (e) SORT USING IN1 IN2 GIVING OUT1 OUT2 with all four in one MULTIPLE FILE TAPE clause (POSITION phrases on three) compiles and OUT2 reads back AAAA BBBB CCCC; (b) the same statement written as a MERGE is refused COBOL6815, the contrast SR6 requires; (c) at --std 2002 the MULTIPLE FILE clause is COBOL0902 (removed). Classes a, d and f do not reach a reel-placement permission. The witness sorts USING and GIVING two files of one reel.

next.reason: 1985: "The files referenced by file-name-2 and file-name-3 may reside on the same multiple file reel."; 2023: "No 2023 SORT syntax rule (SR-14.9.40.3-1 to -15) mentions multiple file reels; SR-8 only bars report and sort-merge files". The 2023 SORT syntax rules cover file-name-2 and file-name-3 but no longer state the multiple-file-reel permission. No candidate carries the multiple-file-reel concept.
